questions.stem: A team seals its `Validator` interface, which has one abstract method `boolean test(Order o)`, with `permits MaxAmount, Blacklist`. Its tests create validators both as `new Validator() { ... }` and as lambdas such as `o -> true`. What happens to those tests?

options.text: Both forms stop compiling, since only the listed types may implement Validator and a lambda can't target it
options.says: javac refuses anonymous classes of a sealed type, and a sealed interface is not a functional interface

options.text: Only the anonymous classes stop compiling, since a lambda isn't a class and is not checked against the list
options.says: a sealed interface is not a functional interface, so the lambda is refused too

options.text: Both forms still compile, since a type without a name can't be listed and is left out of the check
options.says: an anonymous class is refused with 'anonymous classes must not extend sealed classes'

options.text: Both forms still compile but fail when run, since the JVM refuses their classes when it loads them
options.says: javac refuses both forms before anything runs

origin.section: A Sealed Type Names Its Direct Subtypes, and javac Refuses Any Other

questions.stem: Version 3 of a messaging library seals its `Channel` interface with `permits Email, Sms`. An app built against version 2 has its own `record Push(String token) implements Channel`. Ops swaps the version 2 jar for version 3 and restarts the app without rebuilding it. What happens the first time the app creates a `Push`?

options.text: Push fails to load with IncompatibleClassChangeError, since the JVM checks the library's list when it loads Push
options.says: the permitted list is in Channel's class file, and the JVM checks it when it loads a class that implements Channel

options.text: Push fails to load with NoClassDefFoundError, since the new jar no longer holds a type Push was compiled against
options.says: Channel is still in the jar; the JVM refuses Push with IncompatibleClassChangeError

options.text: Push loads and works as before, since the permitted list is a javac check that the class file doesn't keep
options.says: javac stores the list in the class file, and the JVM checks it at load time

options.text: Push loads, and a switch over Channel that meets it throws MatchException, since Push isn't among the permitted types
options.says: Push never loads; the JVM refuses it before any switch sees one

origin.section: The JVM Checks the List When It Loads a Subtype

questions.stem: `Command.java` declares `public sealed interface Command` without a `permits` clause, with three records nested inside it: `Start`, `Stop` and `Pause`. One colleague adds `record Resume() implements Command {}` in another file of the same package. Another nests `record Ping() implements Command {}` inside `Command.java`. Which of the two additions compiles?

options.text: Only Ping, since without a permits clause the list is made of the subtypes declared in Command.java
options.says: javac takes the subtypes declared in the same source file, and nothing else

options.text: Only Resume, since without a permits clause a subtype nested in Command.java must still be named
options.says: the nested records are exactly the ones an omitted permits clause permits

options.text: Both of them, since without a permits clause any type in the same package may implement Command
options.says: a subtype in another file of the same package gets the 'not listed in its permits clause' error

options.text: Neither of them, since without a permits clause the list is fixed to the types there when Command was first written
options.says: the list is read from the file each time it is compiled, so Ping joins it

origin.section: Without permits, the Subtypes in the Same File Are the List

questions.stem: `Account` permits `Checking` and `Savings`. `Savings` is a sealed interface that permits `Fixed` and `Flexible`, and `Checking`, `Fixed` and `Flexible` are records. A helper `walk(type)` prints the type's name and then runs `for (Class<?> c : type.getPermittedSubclasses()) walk(c);` with no other check. What does `walk(Account.class)` do?

options.text: It throws NullPointerException at the first record it reaches, since the method has no array to give for a record
options.says: getPermittedSubclasses() returns null for a type that isn't sealed, and a record isn't

options.text: It prints all five types and returns, since the method gives an empty array for a record, which ends the loop
options.says: the method returns null, not an empty array, for a type that isn't sealed

options.text: It prints Account, Checking and Savings and returns, since the method stops at the subtypes Account names
options.says: the helper calls itself on each subtype; it reaches a record and gets null

options.text: It prints Fixed and Flexible twice, since the method on Account already gives every type below it
options.says: the method lists only the direct subtypes

origin.section: At Run Time, getPermittedSubclasses() Lists the Direct Subtypes Only
